questions.question: What is the expected major product when Ethylene (H2C=CH2) is treated with Benzoyl peroxide initiator (RO•) / heat, pressure?
questions.explanation: Treating Ethylene (H2C=CH2) with Benzoyl peroxide initiator (RO•) / heat, pressure yields Low-density polyethylene (LDPE). Rationale: Peroxide radical initiates chain-growth addition across ethylene double bonds with branching.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of 2-Methylpropene (isobutylene) into Polyisobutylene (butyl rubber)?
questions.explanation: To convert 2-Methylpropene (isobutylene) into Polyisobutylene (butyl rubber), the appropriate reagent is BF3 / H2O (catalytic acid initiator, -80°C). Rationale: Protonation forms 3° carbocation that repeatedly adds isobutylene monomers to form high-MW elastomer.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Styrene (PhCH=CH2) is treated with Butyllithium (BuLi) in THF?
questions.explanation: Treating Styrene (PhCH=CH2) with Butyllithium (BuLi) in THF yields Polystyrene (living anionic polymer). Rationale: Nucleophilic carbanion adds to styrene double bond without termination, forming a monodisperse polymer.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Propene (CH3CH=CH2) into Isotactic polypropylene?
questions.explanation: To convert Propene (CH3CH=CH2) into Isotactic polypropylene, the appropriate reagent is TiCl4 / Al(C2H5)3 (Ziegler-Natta catalyst). Rationale: Titanium coordination site directs monomer insertion so that all methyl groups align on the same side.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Adipic acid + 1,6-Hexanediamine is treated with Heat (280°C, loss of H2O)?
questions.explanation: Treating Adipic acid + 1,6-Hexanediamine with Heat (280°C, loss of H2O) yields Nylon-6,6 (polyamide fiber). Rationale: Stoichiometric condensation of dicarboxylic acid and diamine builds high-tensile polyamide chains.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Dimethyl terephthalate + Ethylene glycol into Polyethylene terephthalate (PET / Dacron)?
questions.explanation: To convert Dimethyl terephthalate + Ethylene glycol into Polyethylene terephthalate (PET / Dacron), the appropriate reagent is Heat / catalyst (loss of 2 CH3OH). Rationale: Transesterification polycondensation links aromatic diesters and diols into recyclable thermoplastic polyester.

questions.question: Which starting material will react with Heat / catalyst to yield Polyurethane polymer as the major product?
questions.explanation: Toluene diisocyanate (TDI) + 1,4-Butanediol reacts with Heat / catalyst to yield Polyurethane polymer. Rationale: Diisocyanate reacts with diol via nucleophilic addition to form repeating urethane (carbamate) linkages.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Norbornene (bicyclo[2.2.1]hept-2-ene) is treated with Grubbs 1st generation ruthenium catalyst?
questions.explanation: Treating Norbornene (bicyclo[2.2.1]hept-2-ene) with Grubbs 1st generation ruthenium catalyst yields Polynorbornene. Rationale: Relief of norbornene ring strain drives ruthenium carbene catalyzed metathesis into linear unsaturated polymer.

questions.question: Which starting material will react with Grubbs catalyst in CH2Cl2 to yield Diethyl cyclopent-3-ene-1,1-dicarboxylate + Ethylene gas as the major product?
questions.explanation: Diethyl diallylmalonate reacts with Grubbs catalyst in CH2Cl2 to yield Diethyl cyclopent-3-ene-1,1-dicarboxylate + Ethylene gas. Rationale: Ruthenium carbene cleaves terminal double bonds and couples internal carbons into a 5-membered ring with ethylene loss.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Unsaturated maleate polyester + Styrene is treated with AIBN initiator / heat?
questions.explanation: Treating Unsaturated maleate polyester + Styrene with AIBN initiator / heat yields Rigid crosslinked fiberglass thermoset resin. Rationale: Radical copolymerization of styrene bridges unsaturated double bonds, forming a permanent 3D network.
